title: Institutional Learning as an Integrative Capability for Sustainable Higher Education: Reconnecting Institutional Research, Quality, Effectiveness, Enhancement, and Planning
content: Higher education institutions have developed extensive infrastructures for producing institutional evidence, assuring quality, evaluating effectiveness, pursuing continuous enhancement, and setting strategic direction. Yet these activities are commonly theorised through partially separate professional and scholarly traditions. This conceptual article addresses the under-specified question of how such differentiated institutional capabilities may become connected through institutional learning. Drawing on higher education scholarship and organisational learning and capability perspectives, the article develops the High Five Framework, which reconceptualises Institutional Research, Quality Assurance, Continuous Quality Enhancement, Institutional Effectiveness, and Planning as complementary institutional capabilities. Institutional Learning is positioned as the higher-order capability through which their relationships become consequential for collective interpretation, action, evaluation, and adaptation. Six theoretically derived propositions render the framework empirically testable. The framework offers an integrative conceptual language for investigating how universities connect distributed evidence, accountability, improvement, resource stewardship, and strategic direction. It contributes to debates on sustainable higher education by conceptualising institutional learning as a potential organisational capability for sustaining educational quality, responsible adaptation, and responsiveness to societal needs. These relationships remain propositions for empirical investigation rather than demonstrated effects.
